seed: Objects of type `marker` under action ACTION2 with touching neighbours [wall] show mixed outcomes: y x3, gone x2, no_change x2. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: the presence, type or relative position of a neighbouring object. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Frame-native rule: floor colour 5; two cyan-10 4x4 blocks move A1/A2 y-/+4, A3 apart / A4 together (mirrored), each only if dest 4x4 is all floor.
Click colour-9 marker arms (blocks->1, marker->11, old active->9); click armed player disarms; other clicks and A5 are no-ops that still tick.
Armed A1-A4 move the active marker 4 cells if its dest 4x4 cell is floor. Hypothesis resolved: marker A2 y = active marker moved, gone = name renumbering after the move, no_change = inactive markers.
HUD: bar of 0s, width 3(n+1)//7, row 0 from right and row 63 from left; n = actions since level start, continuity-gated on last returned frame.
Unconfirmed: win/timeout behaviour and HUD law beyond ~30 actions (longer variants need round(64n/150)).
